title: Squared moment norm of an indicator
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, let $A$ be an event in its product outcome space, and let $p>0$. Then the squared $p$-moment norm of its indicator is $\|\mathbf 1_A\|_{p,P}^{2}=\Pr_P(A)^{2/p}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to one
$A$ is an event in the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, an event $A\subseteq\Omega$, and $p>0$. Then $\|\mathbf1_A\|_{p,P}^2=\Pr_P(A)^{2/p}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\Pr_P(A)=\mathbb E_P\mathbf1_A$, where $\mathbf1_A$ is $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere.
